Consult Summary:
- 61-year-old male presenting with acute onset chest pressure, associated with nausea, diaphoresis, shortness of breath, and left arm/shoulder pain; possible acute coronary syndrome; ambulance arranged for emergency evaluation.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Chest discomfort/pressure, described as “someone sitting on my chest,” onset approximately 2 hours ago while gardening.
- Timeline: Symptoms began a couple of hours prior to consult; still ongoing at time of consult without improvement.
- Exacerbating/initiating/relieving factors: Initiated during light activity (gardening, kneeling); no mention of alleviating factors.
- Associated symptoms: Nausea (no vomiting), diaphoresis (sweaty), shortness of breath, palpitations (heart beating faster than normal due to stress), left arm and shoulder pain.
- Systems review: No prior similar episodes. No mention of jaw or neck pain. Denied diabetes.
- Pertinent negatives: No previous chest pain episodes.
  
Past Medical History:
- Hypertension (high blood pressure).
- No diabetes.
- No documented hyperlipidemia; cholesterol status unknown.

Medications:
- Not documented.

Allergies:
- Aspirin (allergic reaction with mild swelling, not life-threatening, sometimes mild symptoms if taken).

Social History:
- Smoker: 10 cigarettes per day for 15 years.
- Alcohol: Consumes 7–8 pints of beer per week.
- Occupation: Restaurant owner (sushi shop).
- Lives alone at home.
- Reports being overweight.
- No one else present in the house at time of consult.

Family History:
- Father died of a heart attack at approximately age 60.
- Mother with unspecified heart problems.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not documented.
- Physical findings: Not documented (consult was virtual/video; no findings reported).

Investigations:
- None performed during consultation.
- Ambulance team to perform ECG upon arrival.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Possible Acute Coronary Syndrome (e.g., myocardial infarction)
  - Chest pain with left arm/shoulder radiation, associated with nausea, diaphoresis, shortness of breath in a high-risk profile.
  - Ambulance called for emergency transfer and evaluation.
  - Patient advised to keep front door open for ambulance access.
  - Continuous monitoring by clinician until ambulance arrives.
  - Hospital to be informed of aspirin allergy; potential consideration of aspirin will be at hospital discretion.
  - ECG and further management to be done by emergency services.
- General Plan:
  - Family and past medical history relayed to emergency team.
  - Patient advised to communicate aspirin allergy details to admitting providers.

Quality checks (document_quality):

●	Missing but clinically expected elements:
   - Complete medication reconciliation not performed.
   - No vitals or physical exam findings obtained due to virtual/non-physical consult.
   - No documented review of other systems outside those related to presenting complaint.
●	Internal conflicts: None noted.
●	Transcript quality: Good audio; all clinically relevant data extractable.
